title: Brief History of the State of Jammu and Kashmir, 1819–1953
excerpt: A historical overview of the formation, governance and political evolution of the State of Jammu and Kashmir from the Sikh conquest in 1819 to the exile of Maharaja Hari Singh in 1953.
author: Sardar Nasir Aziz Khan

heroImage.caption: Historical flags and symbols of the State of Jammu and Kashmir

body.text: Before the establishment of the State of Jammu and Kashmir in 1846, Kashmir Valley had already experienced major political change. In 1819 the Sikh Empire under Maharaja Ranjit Singh defeated the Afghan Durrani rulers and took control of Kashmir.

From 1819 until 1846 Srinagar and the Kashmir Valley remained under Sikh rule. During this period Gulab Singh served as a prominent Dogra military officer within the Sikh Empire and gradually expanded his authority over Jammu and adjoining hill territories.

Throughout the 1820s and 1830s forces under Gulab Singh and his generals extended control into Ladakh and Baltistan. These campaigns laid the territorial foundations of a larger mountain state that would later include Jammu, Kashmir Valley, Ladakh and the northern frontier regions.

body.caption: Historical flag of Jammu and Kashmir State

body.text: The Treaty of Lahore and Treaty of Amritsar
The First Anglo Sikh War of 1845 to 1846 marked a decisive turning point. The Sikh Empire was defeated by the East India Company resulting in partial subjugation of the Sikh kingdom.

Under the Treaty of Lahore dated 9 March 1846 the Sikh government ceded territories to the British as part of war indemnity arrangements. The British demanded payment of 15 million Nanakshahi rupees as reparations for the cost of the war.

The Lahore Darbar was unable to pay the full amount. Raja of Jammu Gulab Singh agreed to pay seventy five lakh Nanakshahi rupees to the British government. Fifty lakh Nanakshahi were to be paid on ratification of the Treaty and twenty five lakh Nanakshahi before 1 October 1846.
One week later on 16 March 1846 the Treaty of Amritsar was signed between the British Government and Maharaja Gulab Singh.

Through this Treaty the British transferred to Maharaja Gulab Singh all the hilly or mountainous country with its dependencies situated to the eastward of the River Indus and westward of the River Ravi including Chamba.
Gulab Singh became the legitimate ruler and founding father of the State of Jammu and Kashmir. This Treaty formally created the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
The Treaty of Amritsar of 16 March 1846 formally created the State of Jammu and Kashmir.

body.text: Administrative and Legal Development
Under Maharaja Ranbir Singh the administration was consolidated and codified. The Ranbir Penal Code became the foundation of criminal law in the State.
District courts were established and judicial procedures formalized. A functioning judiciary operated across the State and a professional Bar developed in Jammu and Srinagar.
In 1928 during the reign of Maharaja Hari Singh the High Court of Jammu and Kashmir was formally established strengthening judicial authority and appellate review.
Under Maharaja Pratap Singh infrastructure expanded. Roads public buildings and communication systems improved and state departments were modernized.

body.text: Forest Governance and Land Protection
Forest conservation was a key feature of governance. Large tracts of land were declared reserved or protected forests.
Historically more than forty percent of the territory in various regions remained under forest cover particularly in Kashmir Valley and the mountainous belts of Jammu and Ladakh.
Cutting valuable trees such as maple pine and deodar required prior permission from state authorities and unauthorized felling was punishable by law.

body.text: State Subject Rule and Constitutional Reforms
Maharaja Hari Singh who ascended the throne in 1925 introduced major reforms. In 1927 the State Subject Rule was enacted.
It defined hereditary state subjects and granted them first class citizen status. It restricted land ownership government employment and settlement rights to natives of the State.
The purpose was to safeguard land property culture identity history and economic rights from outside acquisition.
In 1934 the Praja Sabha was established as the legislative assembly of Jammu and Kashmir. Members were partly elected and partly nominated.
The right to vote was introduced under a limited franchise system based on property taxation and educational qualifications.
In 1939 the Praja Sabha was expanded increasing elected representation and strengthening legislative functions.

body.text: Events of 1947
In 1947 during the partition of British India into India and Pakistan more than 580 princely states were given the option to join either dominion or remain independent.
Given the State’s complex demography and geography Maharaja Hari Singh chose independence.
On 22 October 1947 Pakistani backed tribal forces entered the State from the northwest and advanced toward Srinagar.
Maharaja Hari Singh approached India for military assistance and signed the Instrument of Provisional Accession limited to defence foreign affairs and communications.
Indian troops were airlifted into Srinagar with assurances to protect life liberty and property of the people of Jammu and Kashmir and repel the invaders.

body.text: United Nations and International Dimension
The United Nations became involved in 1948. Its resolutions and the UNCIP truce agreement called for Pakistan to withdraw forthwith from the territory of the State of Jammu and Kashmir.
India entered Kashmir with promises including protection of life liberty and property and a commitment that the final status would be determined according to the wishes of the people.
The entire State of Jammu and Kashmir remains a disputed territory and its future status is yet to be decided.
The dispute over Jammu and Kashmir is not merely territorial. It concerns the lives and rights of millions of Kashmiris who remain divided.
The European Parliament Resolution on Kashmir adopted on 24 May 2007 was overwhelmingly passed with 522 Members voting in favor.
The Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights issued two significant reports on the situation of human rights in Kashmir in 2018 and 2019.
These international documents confirm that the question of Jammu and Kashmir remains on the global agenda.

From 16 March 1846 until the upheavals of October 1947 the State of Jammu and Kashmir existed as a defined political entity with borders citizenship laws courts a High Court a Bar a legislative assembly known as the Praja Sabha protected forests regulated grazing systems water management and structured governance.
That historical State remains central to understanding the present and future of Jammu and Kashmir.
